method: The default uses the earlier validation period and minimizes mean normalized RMSE across the three indicators and three native horizons for the whole-lake summary. Pooled zone validation breaks ties. Lower is better. Later scores use the same forecast pairs for every candidate.
normalization: Pooled zone RMSE uses training-only within-zone temporal deviation; whole-lake RMSE uses training-only whole-lake temporal deviation. All nine tasks have equal weight within each scope.
limitations: Later periods may already have been reviewed during project development; fresh observations are needed for external validation.
Horizon labels correspond to 1, 2 and 4 satellite reading steps, which may occur at irregular intervals.
Whole-lake comparison lines share origin observation weights on the same eligible zones.
The active forecast model is refitted using all available readings after selection. Its future performance and interval coverage are unknown.
Observations beyond 32 days have not been validated. Prophet models calendar days directly; other models interpolate between the native horizons.
The equal-weight consensus was added after seeing the first retrospective comparison. Its current scores are development evidence, not an unseen test.
Seasonal similarity was added during retrospective development and updates only with observations already recorded at each forecast origin.
Prophet was fitted to observed dates through the fitting cutoff. Its historical predictions use nominal calendar leads, and the same recorded targets as the other candidates.

Whole-lake was chosen as the product selection scope after the initial model comparison, because the dashboard opens to the whole lake. The later period is retrospective model development, not a fresh test of this choice.
